title: Sheaf Operations Exactness Ringed Spaces and Module Pullback

items.title: Direct image of a sheaf along a continuous map
Direct image preserves sheaves and objectwise algebraic structure
items.strategy: An open cover of V in Y pulls back to an open cover of f^{-1}(V) in X, so locality and gluing for F transfer verbatim to f_*F. When F carries groups, rings, or module structure, those operations are already defined on the same section sets over f^{-1}(V), so the sheaf property is still detected on underlying sets.

items.title: Inverse image presheaf and inverse image sheaf
Inverse image is left adjoint to direct image on sheaves
items.strategy: A map from f^{-1}G into F is the same as a map from the neighborhood-colimit presheaf into F, because f^{-1}G is its sheafification. Unwinding the colimit data is equivalent to giving compatible maps G(V) -> F(U) whenever f(U) subseteq V, and this is exactly the same information as a sheaf morphism G -> f_*F.

items.title: The stalk of an inverse image sheaf is the stalk over the image point
items.strategy: The neighborhood-colimit presheaf defining f^{-1}G already has stalk G_{f(x)} at x, because taking the stalk refines neighborhoods of x to neighborhoods of f(x). Sheafification preserves stalks, so the sheafified inverse image has the same stalk.

items.title: Restriction of a sheaf to an open subspace
Extension by zero for abelian sheaves on an open subspace
A skyscraper sheaf of abelian groups at a point
Kernel sheaves are objectwise, while cokernels and images are sheafified
Sheaves of abelian groups, and likewise sheaves of modules on a ringed space, form abelian categories
items.strategy: Kernels are computed sectionwise, while cokernels and images are obtained by sheafifying the presheaf constructions. After taking stalks these become the usual kernel, cokernel, image, and coimage in module categories, so image and coimage agree stalkwise and hence globally.

items.title: Exact sequences of sheaves
A sequence of abelian sheaves is exact exactly when it is exact on every stalk
items.strategy: The kernel, cokernel, image, and coimage constructions commute with passage to stalks, so exactness at a middle sheaf can be tested after taking stalks. Conversely, if every stalk sequence is exact, the stalks of the global image and kernel agree, and a sheaf morphism that is an isomorphism on all stalks is already an isomorphism.

items.title: Global sections are left exact but need not preserve epimorphisms
items.strategy: A kernel sheaf is defined sectionwise, so taking sections over X preserves kernels immediately. Surjectivity can fail because a sheaf epimorphism only guarantees local lifts; the exponential sequence on C supplies a standard global section with no global logarithm.

items.title: Extension by zero is left adjoint to restriction and is exact on abelian sheaves
items.strategy: A map out of j_!F is determined uniquely by what it does on opens contained in U, so it is equivalent to a map F -> j^{-1}G. The stalk description of j_!F is zero outside U and unchanged on U, so an exact sequence on U remains exact after extension by zero because exactness of sheaves is stalkwise.

items.title: A ringed space
Morphisms of ringed spaces
A locally ringed space
Morphisms of locally ringed spaces
A local morphism of stalks induces a residue-field map
items.strategy: If a ring map sends the maximal ideal of the source into the maximal ideal of the target, it descends to the quotient fields by those maximal ideals. Applied to the stalk map f^#_x, this gives the canonical map kappa(f(x)) -> kappa(x).

items.title: Modules on a ringed space
Tensor product of sheaves of modules
The stalk of a tensor product sheaf is the tensor product of the stalks
items.strategy: The tensor-product sheaf is the sheafification of the presheaf U |-> F(U) tensor_{O(U)} G(U). Sheafification does not change stalks, and the directed colimit defining a stalk commutes with the objectwise tensor construction, yielding F_x tensor_{O_x} G_x.

items.title: The internal Hom sheaf of two module sheaves
Pullback of a module along a morphism of ringed spaces
Pullback of modules is left adjoint to pushforward
items.strategy: Write f^*G as O_X tensor_{f^{-1}O_Y} f^{-1}G. Maps from this tensor product to an O_X-module F are equivalent to f^{-1}O_Y-linear maps f^{-1}G -> F, and the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction converts those into O_Y-linear maps G -> f_*F.

items.title: Pullback of modules is right exact, and flat stalk maps make it exact
items.strategy: The inverse-image functor on abelian sheaves is exact, so the only possible failure in f^*G = O_X tensor_{f^{-1}O_Y} f^{-1}G comes from tensoring with O_X. Stalkwise this is ordinary extension of scalars along O_{Y,f(x)} -> O_{X,x}, hence right exact always; if those stalk maps are flat, the stalk sequences stay exact and therefore the pulled-back sheaf sequence is exact.

items.title: A gluing datum for sheaves on an open cover
Compatible local sheaves glue uniquely up to unique isomorphism
items.strategy: Define sections over an open W as families of local sections on W cap U_i that agree under the transition isomorphisms on overlaps. The sheaf axioms for the local pieces show this is a sheaf, and restriction to each U_i recovers the original local sheaf and transition maps.

items.title: Compatible open pieces of ringed or locally ringed spaces glue
items.strategy: First glue the underlying topological spaces by the overlap identifications. Then push each structure sheaf to its image open subset and apply sheaf gluing to the induced ring-sheaf isomorphisms; the glued stalks are the original stalks, so localness is preserved and the usual mapping property follows from the local descriptions.

title: Sheaf Operations Exactness Ringed Spaces and Module Pullback — Examples

items.title: Direct image along an open immersion is restriction-compatible intersection
items.strategy: If i: U hookrightarrow X is the inclusion, then i^{-1}(V) is exactly V cap U for every open V subseteq X. Substituting this into the direct-image definition gives i_*F(V) = F(V cap U), with restrictions inherited from F.

items.title: Extension by zero can be strictly smaller than direct image on a punctured interval
items.strategy: Take U = (-1,0) union (0,1) inside X = (-1,1) and the constant sheaf Z on U. The section that is 1 on both connected components lies in i_*Z(X), but it is not in i_!Z(X) because every neighborhood of 0 meets both components and extension by zero forces the stalk at 0 to vanish.

items.title: A short exact sequence of abelian groups gives a short exact sequence of skyscraper sheaves
items.strategy: Apply the skyscraper construction at a fixed point x to a short exact sequence 0 -> A' -> A -> A'' -> 0. At a point y, the stalk is either the original group sequence if every neighbourhood of y contains x, or the zero sequence once some neighbourhood omits x; stalkwise exactness then proves exactness of the sheaf sequence.

items.title: Global sections need not preserve surjections
items.strategy: Use the exponential sequence of sheaves on the complex plane or punctured complex plane. The sheaf map exp: O -> O^* is surjective only locally, while a global nowhere-vanishing function such as z on C^* has no global logarithm, so the induced map on global sections is not surjective.

items.title: Continuous real-valued functions make a space into a locally ringed space
items.strategy: For any topological space X, the sheaf C^0_X of continuous real-valued functions is a sheaf of rings, so (X, C^0_X) is ringed. The stalk at x consists of germs of continuous functions near x, and the germs vanishing at x form the unique maximal ideal, so these stalks are local rings.

items.title: A morphism of ringed spaces need not be a morphism of locally ringed spaces
items.strategy: Use Vakil's one-point-to-two-point local-spec example: a map Spec k(x) -> Spec k[y]_(y) sending the unique point to the closed point and y to x defines a morphism of ringed spaces, but the induced map on stalks sends the maximal ideal (y) to the unit x in k(x), so it is not local.

items.title: Pullback carries a free module to the corresponding free module
items.strategy: Because inverse image preserves finite direct sums and f^{-1}O_Y becomes an O_X-algebra through f^#, one has f^*(O_Y^n) = O_X tensor_{f^{-1}O_Y} f^{-1}(O_Y^n) isomorphic to n copies of O_X. The case n = 0 is the zero sheaf and the same tensor formula still applies.

items.title: Units satisfying the cocycle law glue local rank-one free modules into a line bundle
items.strategy: On each open U_i take the free rank-one O_{U_i}-module with basis e_i, and on overlaps send e_i to g_{ij} e_j where each g_{ij} is a unit. The cocycle law on triple overlaps is exactly the compatibility needed for a gluing datum of module sheaves, so the glued sheaf is locally free of rank one.

items.title: The objectwise cokernel presheaf can fail to be a sheaf
items.strategy: For the inclusion j: U hookrightarrow X from the punctured interval example, the natural map j_!Z -> j_*Z has objectwise cokernel zero on opens avoiding 0 and Z on opens meeting 0. These local quotients agree on each punctured side but do not glue uniquely across 0, so the presheaf cokernel is not a sheaf until sheafified.
